title: Restoring Brain Protein Menin Reverses Signs of Aging in Mice
summary: Scientists found that restoring the brain protein Menin reversed multiple aging signs in mice, including inflammation, cognitive decline, and physical deterioration. The mechanism involves a disrupted chemical pathway where Menin loss reduces D-serine, an amino acid critical for learning and memory.
takeaways: Menin declines with age in the ventromedial hypothalamus, a brain region controlling metabolism
Menin loss triggers lower bone mass, thinner skin, cognitive decline, and shorter lifespan
D-serine, an amino acid, mediates the connection between Menin and cognitive function
Published March 16, 2023, in PLOS Biology by researchers at Xiamen University

title: Incremental lifestyle improvements in sleep, nutrition, and exercise significantly extend lifespan
summary: A new study finds that modest improvements in sleep quality, diet, and physical activity could substantially extend human lifespan.

title: Semaglutide shown to slow aging and extend lifespan in mice
summary: Semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, extended lifespan by nearly 100 days in older mice while improving memory, muscle function, and reducing aging markers, according to an NIH-funded UC Berkeley study. The drug outperformed calorie restriction in memory and blood-sugar control,
takeaways: Median lifespan extended by nearly 100 days in treated mice
Improved memory, muscle function, blood sugar control, and reduced inflammation
Outperformed calorie restriction in exploratory behavior and spatial memory
Metabolic rate remained unchanged (unlike calorie restriction)
Suggests separate aging pathway beyond appetite suppression

title: Immune receptor blocking may reverse aging in mice
summary: Stanford Medicine researchers found that blocking a single immune receptor on tissue-resident macrophages restored their ability to clear senescent neutrophils, reducing inflammation and maintaining youthful function across multiple organs in aged mice. The intervention protected mice from frailty,
takeaways: Blocking single immune receptor restored cellular cleanup in tissue macrophages
Effects observed across brain, heart, skeletal muscle, liver, spleen, kidney, and colon
Protected mice from frailty, excess fat, and heart trouble
Substantially reduced cognitive decline in aged mice
Published in Science with Katrin Andreasson as senior author

title: Ketogenic diet reduces liver fat by 67% in clinical trial
summary: A ketogenic diet reduced liver fat by 67% in people with obesity and fatty liver disease, significantly outperforming Mediterranean (45% reduction) and low-fat diets in a clinical trial. All three groups lost approximately 10% of body weight over four to five months, with about half of ketogenic par
takeaways: 67% liver fat reduction on ketogenic diet vs. 45% on Mediterranean and low-fat diets
Ketogenic diet: 4% carbs, 73% fat; Mediterranean: 50% carbs, 35% fat; Low-fat: 70% carbs, 15% fat
All groups achieved ~10% body weight loss over 4–5 months
~50% of ketogenic group reversed prediabetes status
Published August 27, 2026, in Cell Metabolism; led by Samuel Klein at Washington University

title: Ketogenic Diet Improves Exercise Response in High Blood Sugar Conditions, Study Shows
summary: Researchers at Virginia Tech found that a high-fat ketogenic diet helped normalize blood sugar in mice and dramatically improved their muscles' ability to use oxygen during exercise. The study, published in Nature Communications on February 25, 2026, suggests that diet and exercise may work synergis
takeaways: Mice on a ketogenic diet normalized blood sugar within one week, eliminating hyperglycemia-like conditions
Ketogenic diet caused muscle remodeling, increasing oxidative capacity and slow-twitch endurance fibers
High blood sugar normally impairs the body's ability to gain oxygen-efficiency benefits from exercise, which the keto diet appeared to reverse
Study led by Sarah Lessard at Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute

title: GLP-1 drugs linked to nutritional deficiencies in nearly 1 in 6 children
summary: A study of 2,031 children on GLP-1 medications found that 16.8% developed a nutritional deficiency within one year, with vitamin D deficiency most common at 12.4%. Only 5% received nutritional counseling within 30 days of treatment initiation.
takeaways: 16.8% of children (nearly 1 in 6) diagnosed with nutritional deficiency within first year
Vitamin D deficiency most prevalent at 12.4%; iron and calcium also concerning for adolescent skeletal health
Only 5% received nutritional counseling within 30 days; <25% within 6 months
Liraglutide accounted for 78.6% of prescriptions; dulaglutide 10.4%; semaglutide 9.1%

title: Large review finds calcium and vitamin D supplements provide little fracture prevention benefit in most older adults
summary: A comprehensive review of 69 trials involving nearly 154,000 older adults found that calcium and vitamin D supplements—alone or combined—provide little to no meaningful fracture or fall prevention benefit. The findings challenge routine supplementation recommendations and suggest exercise-based stra
takeaways: 153,902 adults analyzed across 69 randomized controlled trials
High certainty evidence for vitamin D alone (36 trials, 92,045 participants)
High certainty evidence for combination therapy (15 trials, 51,126 participants)
Published in The BMJ
Balance and resistance exercise may be more effective alternatives

title: Diet Changes Reverse Biological Age in Older Adults Within 4 Weeks
summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney found that older adults aged 65–75 who shifted their diet toward lower fat and higher carbohydrates showed reduced biological age markers within four weeks. The omnivorous high-carbohydrate diet produced the strongest results, measured across 20 biomarkers inc
takeaways: 104 participants aged 65–75
Omnivorous high-carbohydrate diet showed strongest results
Biological age assessed using 20 biomarkers
Changes detected within four weeks
Study preliminary; longer-term persistence and disease-risk reduction remain unknown

title: Study identifies optimal whole grain intake of 4-6 servings daily for heart health
summary: A meta-analysis of 87 randomized controlled trials found that consuming 4–6 servings of whole grains daily (60–100 grams dry weight) produces the strongest improvements in cardiovascular risk factors including cholesterol, blood pressure, and inflammation.
takeaways: 4–6 servings daily optimal for heart health benefits
60–100 grams per day (dry weight)
Improvements in weight, cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides, blood glucose
Benefits observed at 30–40 grams but plateau at higher levels
Meta-analysis of 87 clinical trials, over 6,500 participants
Published September 15, 2026 in European Heart Journal

title: Lifestyle program improves cognition 55% more than basic health advice
summary: A two-year study of older adults at dementia risk across 11 Latin American countries found that structured lifestyle programs combining exercise, diet, cognitive training, and social engagement produced 55% greater cognitive improvements than standard health advice. takeaways: 55% greater cognitive improvement versus general health advice
Two-year LatAm-FINGERS study across 11 Latin American countries
Combines exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, social engagement
Results published in The Lancet; presented at AAIC 2026 London
Strongest benefits with regular coaching and structured support
Culturally adapted: salsa/tango, MIND diet with avocado/quinoa/chia

title: Long-term melatonin use linked to 90% higher heart failure risk
summary: A large preliminary study found chronic insomnia patients using melatonin long-term had approximately 90% higher risk of developing heart failure over five years. The findings raise questions about the long-term safety of the over-the-counter supplement, which lacks FDA regulation for strength and p
takeaways: 90% elevated heart failure risk over 5 years in chronic melatonin users with insomnia
Associations also found with heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality
Data from TriNetX Global Research Network covering electronic health records
Study does not establish causation
OTC melatonin supplements lack FDA regulation for potency consistency

title: Ultra-processed foods linked to fat buildup in thigh muscles affecting knee health
summary: A study of 615 adults found that consuming more ultra-processed foods was associated with increased fat accumulation within thigh muscles, independent of calorie intake or exercise.

summary: Researchers found that oxalates in foods like spinach and almonds may aggravate gut inflammation in people with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

summary: A small study found that eating only during an 8-hour window (noon to 8 p.m.) improved blood sugar control in adults with Type 1 diabetes and obesity.

summary: Researchers found that elevated blood tyrosine levels are associated with reduced life expectancy in men, based on a study of over 270,000 people.

title: Obesity Memory in Immune Cells Persists 5–10 Years After Weight Loss
summary: Research shows obesity leaves a lasting molecular imprint on immune cells that may persist for 5 to 10 years after weight loss, potentially explaining why some health risks remain elevated.

title: Sucralose and Stevia May Have Multi-Generational Effects on Gut Health
summary: Research shows that the zero-calorie sweeteners sucralose and stevia alter the gut microbiome in mice with effects that may persist across generations.

title: Researchers develop bioavailable spirulina with natural vitamin B12

summary: GLP-1 drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy may raise hair-loss risk by 7% in genetically susceptible men through a biological mechanism beyond rapid weight loss.

title: Sorbitol sugar substitute may convert to fructose in liver
